author: larrypnp
caption: If an emergency happened today, could your family function independently for the next 72 hours,whether you stayed home or had to leave? Build your plan around the essentials: ✅ Water ✅ Food requiring little or no preparation ✅ Prescription medications ✅ First-aid supplies ✅ Clothing and sturdy footwear ✅ Flashlights and backup power ✅ Emergency communications ✅ Important documents and contact information ✅ Supplies for infants, older adults, or family members with special needs ✅ Food, water, medications, carriers, and other supplies for your pets Remember: water is heavy. Don’t expect one backpack to carry everything your entire family needs. Keep additional supplies at home, and prepare portable bags with the essentials you would need if you had to leave quickly. Your primary plan may be to shelter in place, but you must also be ready to evacuate when conditions become unsafe or local authorities tell you to leave. The goal isn’t to pack everything you own. It’s to protect what your family needs most. author: kelseymayvandy
caption: 🚨 DAY 14 OF THE POWER OUT PREPARED PLAN! ⚡ Would you know what to do if the power suddenly went out? Whether it lasts a few hours or several days, knowing what to do FIRST can make all the difference! Here are the first 7 things I would do during a power outage! 👇 1️⃣ FIND OUT WHAT’S HAPPENING 📱 Check with your power company for outage updates, estimated restoration times, and any emergency alerts in your area. 2️⃣ GET YOUR BACKUP LIGHTING 🔦 Grab your headlamps, flashlights, and battery-powered lanterns. Headlamps are my personal favorite because they keep your hands free! 3️⃣ MAKE SURE EVERYONE IS SAFE ❤️ Check on your family, children, pets, and anyone who may need extra assistance. 4️⃣ KEEP YOUR REFRIGERATOR AND FREEZER CLOSED! 🧊 An unopened refrigerator will generally keep food safe for about 4 hours. A full freezer can maintain safe temperatures for approximately 48 hours (24 hours if half-full). Every time you open the door, you lose precious cold air! 5️⃣ LOCATE YOUR EMERGENCY SUPPLIES 🎒 Gather your 72-hour kits, emergency food, drinking water, medications, first aid supplies, and backup power sources. Everything should be easily accessible! 6️⃣ STORE EXTRA WATER! 💧 If your tap water is still running and safe, fill clean drinking-water containers and your bathtub for non-drinking uses. This is especially important during an extended outage! Depending on your water system, you could lose running water too. 7️⃣ DESIGNATE A HOT OR COOL ROOM! 🌡️ Depending on the weather, choose one room where your family can gather to conserve warmth or stay cooler. Close off unused rooms when appropriate and use safe heating or cooling methods. Never use a gas stove, grill, or outdoor generator to heat your home. ❤️ BEING PREPARED ISN’T ABOUT FEAR. IT’S ABOUT PEACE OF MIND! We’ve covered SO much over these past 14 days, and I hope this series has helped you feel more confident and prepared to protect your family! 👇 NOW I WANT TO HEAR FROM YOU! 👍 Drop a THUMBS UP if this series has been helpful! 💬 Have questions about power outages or emergency preparedness? Leave them below! I’ll be diving deeper into your questions! 🎉 AND STAY TUNED! A MASSIVE GIVEAWAY IS COMING YOUR WAY! You won’t want to miss this one! Save this post so you know exactly what to do when the lights go out! 🔦❤️
